card.title: Nintendo Switch M92T36 Power Management IC Test & Voltage Checks

claims.statement: M92T36 pin 5 input line should measure between 3v to 6v; 0v or less indicates a short on that line.
claims.evidence: Measurement on M92T36 pin 5 (or the capacitor on the end of its trace) with the multimeter set to DC voltage.
claims.quote: Put the main board back in the switch frame, you don’t need to connect anything, just connect the battery. After connecting the battery, click on the power button, put the multimeter to DC Voltage and then put the black

claims.statement: M92T36 pin 6 output voltage should measure between 3v to 6v; 0v means the M92T36 is bad.
claims.evidence: Measurement on M92T36 pin 6 (or the capacitor on the end of its trace) with DC voltage mode.
claims.quote: Now you need to check the output voltage that is pin 6, with the black probe on ground and with the red probe touch the pin 6 or the capacitor on the end of the trace... and its suppose to have between 3v to 6v. 0v in pi

claims.statement: BQ24193 pin 1 VBus should read high 5v to 15v depending on the charger.
claims.evidence: DC voltage measurement on BQ24193 pin 1 when a charger is plugged in.
claims.quote: Pin 1 VBus should be high 5v-15v depending on charger

claims.statement: BQ24193 pin 2 should read low when using the official Nintendo charger.
claims.evidence: DC voltage measurement on BQ24193 pin 2.
claims.quote: pin 2 if using the nintendo charger this pin should read low

claims.statement: BQ24193 pin 3 should be low at 0v.
claims.evidence: DC voltage measurement on BQ24193 pin 3.

claims.statement: BQ24193 pin 4 should be low if charging is in progress; high if complete/disabled; alternating if there is a fault.
claims.evidence: DC voltage measurement on BQ24193 pin 4.
claims.quote: pin 4 should be low if charge in progress, if this pin is high charge is complete or disabled, if this pin is alternating from low to high this could indicate a fault.

procedure: Unplug the battery and check the USB charger fuse in continuity mode.
Check BQ24193 input/output voltages and charge behavior after charging for 30 minutes.
Inspect for shorts on the motherboard capacitors and M92T36 pins using continuity mode with the battery unplugged.
Reinstall the motherboard into the frame with just the battery connected, power on, and test M92T36 pin 5 and pin 6 input/output voltages in DC voltage mode.
Inspect screen and backlight ribbon cables and connectors if voltages are correct.
If the screen remains black, attempt RCM mode and payload injection or inspect the PI3USB30532 chip and surrounding passives.
tools: precision multimeter probe or soldered paper pin
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Measuring live pins on the M92T36 requires very fine probes or a soldered paper pin to the red probe; take care not to slip and cause shorts.
card.caveats: In-circuit measured values should be used for comparison; definitive verification often requires removing components to test out-of-circuit.
